detect.auth_fix_hint: start a local server: uv run mlx_lm.server --model <hf-id> --port 8080 (the adapter talks to $MLX_BASE_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1)

read-only.native: structural: mlx_lm.server only generates text and this adapter wires NO tools, so file reads/writes and shell exec are impossible regardless of posture — read-only is absolute, not a denyable config

workspace.native: no-op: MLX has no write/exec surface to grant; workspace is advisory only (same text-only backend as read-only)

dangerous.native: no-op: nothing to bypass; MLX cannot act on the filesystem or shell — a dangerous posture grants no additional capability

notes.path: Path B: dedicated mlx adapter, single-user-message one-shot against a local mlx_lm.server OpenAI endpoint. Deliberately NO agentic system prompt (unlike Path A opencode:mlx/*), which is what keeps small-local-model code output uncorrupted — OpenCode's tool-schema-heavy system prompt induced a 7B-4bit to escape quotes in reproduced code; the raw server does not. See retrospectives/232-external-agent-delegation.md.
notes.stop_injection: the client always sends stop:[<|im_end|>] (override via $MLX_STOP in adapter.sh / --stop) because mlx_lm.server (>=0.31.3) can leak the chat stop token into message content (known upstream: ml-explore/mlx-lm #973, #875), which would break downstream answer-contract parsing.
notes.concurrency: fanout_safe:false — one mlx_lm.server serves ONE model and ~32 GB unified memory cannot hold two large models concurrently, so the council must assess MLX sequentially (assess.sh --max-concurrent 1). A single MLX handle inside an otherwise-hosted fan-out is fine; two concurrent MLX handles are not.
notes.hardware_risk: on a 32GB unified-memory Apple Silicon laptop, a 32B-parameter dense model (e.g. Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct-4bit) is at real risk of a kernel panic (reboot) under GPU/unified-memory pressure, especially on long-context items — observed twice during council-tool-use-assessment work (#235), with panic reasons in the IOGPU/Metal memory subsystem (IOGPUMemory.cpp / IOGPUGroupMemory.cpp) rather than a catchable app-level OOM. The MoE Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B variants (~3B active params) are lighter in practice despite the similar-looking parameter count and did not trigger this. Prefer 30B-A3B or smaller dense models (7B/14B) for routine/unattended fleet runs; if 32B must be exercised, run it in isolation with nothing else in flight and tolerance for an unplanned reboot. See mlx-panic-report.sh / mlx-server-run.sh for post-mortem tooling — they diagnose which job/item was in flight but do not prevent the panic.
notes.resume: mlx_lm.server is stateless (no server-side sessions). On resume the client reconstructs conversation history from the engine's own per-turn files (turn-NNN.prompt.txt -> user, turn-NNN.last-message.txt -> assistant) under --history-dir, and adapter_capture_session_id synthesizes a deterministic local id (mlx-<handle>) on turn 1 so the engine's resume gate is satisfied.
notes.binary_location: the 'mlx-chat' client ships in this adapter directory and is NOT expected on PATH in production; the adapter resolves it via $MLX_CHAT_BIN override, then PATH (where the test mock lives), then $ADAPTER_DIR/mlx-chat. The engine's own best-effort `binary --version` version probe is non-fatal when mlx-chat is not on PATH.
